current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2023-2024 and 2025-2026 Regular Sessions of the Pennsylvania General Assembly. Codified/compiled statute available: the official compiled text of the Right-to-Know Law, Act 3 of 2008 (65 P.S. §§ 67.101–67.3104), on legis.state.pa.us, which incorporates amendments through Act 29 of 2023 (Nov. 16, 2023 — Chapter 15 State-related institutions only); §§ 701–706, 901–905, 1101, 1307 and 1308 carry no amendment notes and stand as enacted in 2008. Recency: no 2024–2026 enacted amendment to the fee/payment sections was found; palegis.us lists only pending 2025-2026 bills (HB 91, HB 197, HB 279, HB 802, HB 834, SB 226, SB 686 — exemptions, definitions, penalties; none seen touching § 1307). Delegated instrument: the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (statutory delegation § 1307(b)(1)(i) for Commonwealth and local agencies) was opened on the OOR web page and as PDF; the web page states adoption Dec. 30, 2024 while the PDF header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022' — contents identical; flagged. Guidance-vs-law gaps: the categorical bar on search/retrieval fees and staff time, the $1.00/disc CD cap, the e-mail no-fee rule and the $5 certification figure are OOR schedule/guidance constructions of § 1307, not statute text; the certification $5 is expressly a recommendation on the statute's 'reasonable fees' standard. Three OOR advisory opinions bearing on fees were opened (2009 e-transmission; 2016 payment for prior unretrieved records; 2022 policies limiting number of requests); the two older ones are scanned images read by OCR. Estimate calibration out of scope per run parameters. Municipal scope: every figure resolved binds local agencies (municipalities) — the RTKL runs one regime for Commonwealth and local agencies; judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees.

No 'deemed withdrawn after N days' rule.

new_rules.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — no fee for search, retrieval, staff time or the response letter
new_rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for searching for or retrieving records; an agency may not charge staff time or salary for complying with a request; no fee may be charged for the agency's response letter.
new_rules.trigger: Any request
new_rules.source_language: Fee Limitations: Except as otherwise provided by statute, the RTKL states that no other fees may be imposed unless the agency necessarily incurs costs for complying with the request, and such fees must be reasonable. No fee may be imposed for an agency’s review of a record to determine whether the record is a public record subject to access under the RTKL. No fee may be charged for searching for or retrieval of documents. An agency may not charge staff time or salary for complying with a RTK request. No fee may be charged for an agency’s response letter.

new_rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by statute, no other fees may be imposed unless the agency necessarily incurs costs for complying with the request, and such fees must be reasonable.
new_rules.source_authority: 65 P.S. § 67.1307(g) (first sentence)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (no amendment to § 1307 through Act 29 of 2023; none found for 2024–2026)
new_rules.notes: PA-0042 carries only the second sentence of § 1307(g); this row carries the first. No request-level dollar cap exists in the RTKL.

new_rules.legal_concept: All applicable fees must be paid to receive access
new_rules.atomic_rule: All applicable fees shall be paid in order for the requester to receive access to the requested record.
new_rules.trigger: Fees are due on a request
new_rules.source_language: All applicable fees shall be paid in order to receive access to the record requested.
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: OOR schedule adds: 'Once the request is fulfilled and prepared for release, the OOR recommends that the agency obtain payment prior to releasing the records.' Prepayment of an estimate is separately permitted by § 1307(h) when expected fees exceed $100 (PA-0046).

new_rules.legal_concept: Refusal to pay applicable fees is a ground for a 30-day extension; deemed denial thereafter
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the requester refuses to pay applicable fees, the open-records officer may extend the response time by written notice within five business days; if the expected response date is more than 30 days after the five business days the request is deemed denied unless the requester agrees in writing to the extension.
new_rules.trigger: Requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by the act
new_rules.clock_spec: up to 30 calendar-days beyond the 5 business-day response period from receipt by the open-records officer; deemed denied the day after the noticed date if not answered
new_rules.source_language: (a) Determination.--Upon receipt of a written request for access, the open-records officer for an agency shall determine if one of the following applies: ... (6) the requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by this act; ... (b) Notice.-- (1) Upon a determination that one of the factors listed in subsection (a) applies, the open-records officer shall send written notice to the requester within five business days of receipt of the request for access under subsection (a). (2) The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available. If the date that a response is expected to be provided is in excess of 30 days, following the five business days allowed for in section 901, the request for access shall be deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to an extension to the date specified in the notice. (3) If the requester agrees to the extension, the request shall be deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: This is the RTKL's only clock effect tied to nonpayment: nonpayment does not toll the clock; it is an extension ground with a hard 30-day outer limit absent written agreement.

new_rules.legal_concept: Extension notice must include an estimate of applicable fees
new_rules.atomic_rule: Every § 902 extension notice must include an estimate of the applicable fees that will be owed when the record becomes available.
new_rules.trigger: Open-records officer sends a § 902 extension notice
new_rules.source_language: The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available.
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: No dollar or hour threshold triggers an estimate; the estimate is a required element of any extension notice. The $100 figure in § 1307(h) is a prepayment threshold, not an estimate-notice threshold.

new_rules.legal_concept: Unretrieved copies may be disposed of after 60 days; fees paid retained
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the agency's response states that copies are available for delivery at its office and the requester fails to retrieve them within 60 days of the response, the agency may dispose of the unretrieved copies and retain any fees paid to date.
new_rules.trigger: Response says copies available at agency office; requester does not retrieve within 60 days
new_rules.clock_spec: 60 days from the agency's response (statute says 'days'; not stated as business days)
new_rules.source_language: If an agency response to a requester states that copies of the requested records are available for delivery at the office of an agency and the requester fails to retrieve the records within 60 days of the agency's response, the agency may dispose of any copies which have not been retrieved and retain any fees paid to date.
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: Trigger is failure to retrieve (which includes failure to pay, since § 901 conditions access on payment). Discretionary ('may dispose').

new_rules.legal_concept: Access may be withheld until fees owed from an earlier request are paid
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may process a new request but withhold access until all applicable fees, including fees owed for earlier requests (even where the earlier copies were never retrieved), are paid; it must still respond or issue an extension notice within five business days and should state the past-due fees as a reason in its response.
new_rules.trigger: Requester owes fees from a prior RTKL request
new_rules.source_language: In Department of Transportation v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355, 363 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012), the Commonwealth Court held that, when a requester "owes money for an agency’s fulfillment of an earlier request ... Section 901 of the RTKL permits an agency to process the request but to withhold access to the request until all applicable fees, including fees for earlier requests, are paid" ... Based on the pertinent language in Drack in conjunction with Sections 901 and 905 of the RTKL, it can be discerned that agencies may deny access to records sought in RTKL requests based on a requester’s outstanding fees stemming from a prior RTKL request. This would apply even where the requester never retrieved the records, because the agency, in responding to the prior request, had been required to produce physical copies of the requested records. However, even if fees are owed in response to a prior RTKL request, agencies must still timely process future RTKL requests. ... Further, if an agency chooses to deny a request due to fees owed as a result of a prior request, the agency should raise all applicable reasons for denying access, including the fact that past due fees are owed, in its response.
new_rules.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Jan. 12, 2016 (Requiring Payment When A Requester Has Not Retrieved Records From A Prior Request), applying Dep't of Transp. v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012), 65 P.S. §§ 67.901, 67.905
new_rules.effective_status: Current (advisory; OOR states advisory opinions are not binding and may be superseded)
new_rules.notes: Scanned PDF read via OCR — quotation transcribed from the OCR text; verify against the PDF image. The same opinion notes (footnote 1) that fees set in an agency response may be appealed to the OOR within 15 business days under § 1101 (citing Prison Legal News v. OOR, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010)).

new_rules.legal_concept: Complex data sets may be priced at market value, except for news media and nonprofit educational research
new_rules.atomic_rule: For complex and extensive data sets (e.g., GIS or integrated property assessment lists) copying fees may be based on the reasonable market value of the same or closely related data sets, but not for a request by a person employed by or connected with a news organization for publication/broadcast or by a nonprofit organization for educational research, whose fees remain subject to the ordinary duplication rules.
new_rules.trigger: Request for a complex and extensive data set
new_rules.source_language: (4) The following apply to complex and extensive data sets, including geographic information systems or integrated property assessment lists. (i) Fees for copying may be based on the reasonable market value of the same or closely related data sets. (ii) Subparagraph (i) shall not apply to: (A) a request by an individual employed by or connected with a newspaper or magazine of general circulation, weekly publication, press association or radio or television station, for the purpose of obtaining information for publication or broadcast; or (B) a request by a nonprofit organization for the conduct of educational research. (iii) Information obtained under subparagraph (ii) shall be subject to paragraphs (1), (2) and (3).
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: The RTKL's only purpose-sensitive fee rule; there is no commercial-purpose surcharge, and § 703 / § 1308(2) bar requiring a statement of purpose. Secondary concept fee.commercial_charge (inverse: exemption for media/nonprofit-educational requesters). See also OOR § 1307(e) approvals list for county GIS/assessment data fees.

new_rules.legal_concept: All schedule fees may be waived at the agency's discretion
new_rules.atomic_rule: All fees established in the OOR schedule may be waived at the discretion of the agency.
new_rules.trigger: Agency elects to waive fees
new_rules.source_language: Fees May Be Waived: All fees established herein may be waived at the discretion of the agency.
new_rules.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
new_rules.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
new_rules.notes: Extends § 1307(f) (duplication-fee waiver, PA-0043) to every schedule fee. No mandatory waiver ground, no purpose statement (barred by § 703 / § 1308(2)). Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

new_rules.legal_concept: Enhanced electronic access user fees — permitted methods, must be reasonable, OOR-approved, no exclusion or profit
new_rules.atomic_rule: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access beyond the inspection/duplication access the act requires, it may set user fees for that access (flat rate, subscription, per-transaction, cumulative-time or other reasonable method), but the fees must be reasonable, must be approved by the Office of Open Records, and may not be set with the intent or effect of excluding persons from access or creating profit for the agency.
new_rules.trigger: Agency offers optional enhanced electronic access
new_rules.source_language: The user fees for enhanced electronic access may be a flat rate, a subscription fee for a period of time, a per-transaction fee, a fee based on the cumulative time of system access or any other reasonable method and any combination thereof. The user fees for enhanced electronic access must be reasonable, must be approved by the Office of Open Records and may not be established with the intent or effect of excluding persons from access to records or duplicates thereof or of creating profit for the agency.
new_rules.source_authority: 65 P.S. § 67.1307(e) (second and third sentences)
new_rules.effective_status: Current
new_rules.notes: Amends PA-0045, which quoted only the first sentence and omitted the OOR pre-approval requirement. OOR publishes an Enhanced Electronic Access Fee Application Form and a list of approvals (e.g., Berks County delinquent tax data, Oct. 9, 2025). Not a general programming/labor rate — approvals are agency-specific.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fees set in an agency response may be appealed to the OOR within 15 business days
new_rules.atomic_rule: A requester may appeal the fees set forth in an agency's response to the Office of Open Records within 15 business days under § 1101.
new_rules.trigger: Agency response imposes fees the requester disputes
new_rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from the agency response (§ 1101 appeal window)
new_rules.source_language: The OOR notes that the Requester in this scenario could appeal the fees set forth in the agency’s response within 15 business days pursuant to 65 P.S. § 67.1101. See Prison Legal News v. Office of Open Records, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010); State Employees’ Ret. Sys. v. Office of Open Records, 10 A.3d 358 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010).
new_rules.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Jan. 12, 2016, n.1 (citing 65 P.S. § 67.1101 and Prison Legal News v. OOR, 992 A.2d 942 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2010))
new_rules.effective_status: Current (advisory)

new_rules.legal_concept: OOR Advisory Opinion — no per-page charge for e-mailing a record that already exists electronically
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a document already exists in electronic format and can be attached to an e-mail, an agency may not charge for copies; a copy charge is permissible only where the agency had to duplicate the original on a traditional copier (e.g., copying a bound volume in order to scan it), because fees are based on actual out-of-pocket expenses for paper, toner, etc.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for records by e-mail attachment
new_rules.source_language: When a document already exists in electronic format and can be attached to an email, it is not permissible to charge for copies, because none were required to be made in order to fulfill the request. However, in the example you provided — a request for a collective bargaining agreement - it would be appropriate to charge for copies if a bound volume is copied and then a PDF or other attachment is made from scanning those copies. In that instance, the agency has incurred the expense of copying the bound volume in order to make a document capable of being scanned, attached to an email and transmitted electronically. It is only permissible to charge for copies if it is required to duplicate the original using a traditional copier as fees are based upon actual out-of-pocket expenses for paper, toner, etc.
new_rules.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion, Mar. 26, 2009 (Charging for Electronically Transmitted Public Records)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (advisory; the OOR schedule now states the rule directly)
new_rules.notes: Scanned PDF read via OCR — verify against the image. Superseded in practice by the schedule line 'Records Delivered via Email or Other Electronic Method — No additional fee may be imposed' (PA-9004); retained because it states the actual-out-of-pocket rationale.

new_rules.legal_concept: Duplication fees for Commonwealth and local agencies are established by the Office of Open Records; reasonable, based on prevailing local rates; may reflect regional differences
new_rules.atomic_rule: Fees for duplication (photocopying, printing from electronic media or microfilm, copying onto electronic media, facsimile/electronic transmission and other duplication) by Commonwealth and local agencies are established by the Office of Open Records, must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities, and for local agencies may reflect regional price differences.
new_rules.trigger: Requester seeks duplication of records
new_rules.source_language: (1) Fees for duplication by photocopying, printing from electronic media or microfilm, copying onto electronic media, transmission by facsimile or other electronic means and other means of duplication shall be established: (i) by the Office of Open Records, for Commonwealth agencies and local agencies; (ii) by each judicial agency; and (iii) by each legislative agency. (2) The fees must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities. (3) Fees for local agencies may reflect regional price differences.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (no amendment to § 1307 through Act 29 of 2023; none found for 2024–2026)

applicability_notes: The RTKL runs a single fee regime for 'Commonwealth agencies' and 'local agencies' (§ 1307(b)(1)(i)); municipalities are local agencies, so every OOR schedule figure binds them. Judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees (§ 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii)) and are outside this product's scope. applies_to is recorded as all_public_bodies with that caveat.
§ 1307(b)(3) permits local-agency fees to 'reflect regional price differences', but the OOR schedule publishes one uniform set of ceilings; no regional variant was found.

Statutory fees in other laws (e.g., 75 Pa.C.S. § 3751(b)(2) accident reports up to $15; 42 P.S. § 21051 recorder of deeds) control over the OOR schedule for those record types — record-specific overrides, not municipal defaults.
Law-enforcement audio/video recordings are governed by Act 22 of 2017 (42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 67A), not the RTKL; that act allows undefined 'reasonable fees' — a separate request path.

The OOR's staff-time / search-and-retrieval prohibition is guidance construing § 1307(g); it is applied by the OOR as the appeals body for local agencies, so it operates as binding for municipalities in practice.
material_negatives: No free page allowance, no free labor hours, no requestor-period free time (labor is not chargeable at all).
No estimate-notice dollar/hour threshold, no requester response window for estimates, no revised-estimate/variance rule, no estimate validity period, no overrun re-issue rule.
No deposit-cap percentage (prepayment is of the estimate itself, permitted only above $100).
No request-level dollar cap, no de-minimis threshold, no minimum fee.
No commercial-purpose surcharge; purpose may not be required (§ 703, § 1308(2)).
No fee forfeiture for late response (late = deemed denial).
No aggregation threshold for repeat requests; § 1308(1) forbids policies limiting the number of records/requests.
No electronic-payment-method requirement in the RTKL.
No 2024–2026 enacted amendment to § 1307 or §§ 901–905 found; only pending 2025-2026 bills.
